A reference .NET application implementing an e-commerce website using a services-based architecture using [.NET Aspire](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspire/).

![eShop Reference Application architecture diagram](img/eshop_architecture.png)

![eShop homepage screenshot](img/eshop_homepage.png)

## Getting Started

This version of eShop is based on .NET 9. 

Previous eShop versions:
* [.NET 8](https://github.com/dotnet/eShop/tree/release/8.0)

### Prerequisites

- Clone the eShop repository: https://github.com/dotnet/eshop
- [Install & start Docker Desktop](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/)

#### Windows with Visual Studio
- Install [Visual Studio 2022 version 17.10 or newer](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/vs/).
  - Select the following workloads:
    - `ASP.NET and web development` workload.
    - `.NET Aspire SDK` component in `Individual components`.
    - Optional: `.NET Multi-platform App UI development` to run client apps

Or

- Run the following commands in a Powershell & Terminal running as `Administrator` to automatically configure your environment with the required tools to build and run this application. (Note: A restart is required and included in the script below.)

```powershell
install-Module -Name Microsoft.WinGet.Configuration -AllowPrerelease -AcceptLicense -Force
$env:Path = [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","Machine") + ";" + [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","User")
get-WinGetConfiguration -file .\.configurations\vside.dsc.yaml | Invoke-WinGetConfiguration -AcceptConfigurationAgreements
```

Or

- From Dev Home go to `Machine Configuration -> Clone repositories`. Enter the URL for this repository. In the confirmation screen look for the section `Configuration File Detected` and click `Run File`.

#### Mac, Linux, & Windows without Visual Studio
- Install the latest [.NET 9 SDK](https://dot.net/download?cid=eshop)

##### Install Visual Studio Code and related extensions

## What kind of system this is

**eShop is a .NET Aspire–orchestrated, microservices-based e-commerce reference application** ("AdventureWorks"): a set of independently-hosted ASP.NET Core services that talk over HTTP, gRPC, and a RabbitMQ integration-event bus, plus two .NET MAUI client apps. It is an app, not a library — 19 projects in `eShop.slnx`, described in `README.md:1-3` as "A reference .NET application implementing an e-commerce website using a services-based architecture using .NET Aspire". It targets `net10.0` (e.g. `src/Ordering.API/Ordering.API.csproj:4`).

## The single runnable entry point

**`src/eShop.AppHost` is the one thing you run.** It is an Aspire AppHost (`src/eShop.AppHost/eShop.AppHost.csproj:1` — `Sdk="Aspire.AppHost.Sdk/13.2.0"`, `OutputType=Exe`), started via `dotnet run --project src/eShop.AppHost/eShop.AppHost.csproj` (`README.md:72-75`) or by setting it as the startup project in `eShop.Web.slnf` (`README.md:67-70`). Everything else is composed by `builder.Build().Run()` at `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:103`.

## Processes that start when the solution runs

**Nine .NET projects**, each `AddProject`-ed in `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs` (and each project-referenced from `src/eShop.AppHost/eShop.AppHost.csproj:21-31`):

| Resource name | Project | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| `identity-api` (`Program.cs:23`) | Identity.API | ASP.NET Core MVC + Duende IdentityServer; `AddIdentityServer` at `src/Identity.API/Program.cs:18`, auto-migrates `identitydb` (`src/Identity.API/Program.cs:12`) |
| `basket-api` (`Program.cs:30`) | Basket.API | gRPC service — `app.MapGrpcService<BasketService>()` (`src/Basket.API/Program.cs:12`), backed by Redis |
| `catalog-api` (`Program.cs:36`) | Catalog.API | Minimal-API web API over Postgres/pgvector, with optional AI semantic search |
| `ordering-api` (`Program.cs:40`) | Ordering.API | Minimal-API web API, DDD/CQRS with MediatR pipeline behaviors (`LoggingBehavior`, `ValidatorBehavior`, `TransactionBehavior`); owns the EF migrations |
| `order-processor` (`Program.cs:46`) | OrderProcessor | Background worker — `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Worker` (`src/OrderProcessor/OrderProcessor.csproj:1`), runs `GracePeriodManagerService` as a hosted service (`src/OrderProcessor/Extensions/Extensions.cs:18`) |
| `payment-processor` (`Program.cs:51`) | PaymentProcessor | Event-driven worker; its only job is subscribing to `OrderStatusChangedToStockConfirmedIntegrationEvent` (`src/PaymentProcessor/Program.cs:5-6`) |
| `webhooks-api` (`Program.cs:54`) | Webhooks.API | Versioned minimal-API for webhook subscriptions (`src/Webhooks.API/Program.cs:19-21`) |
| `webapp` (`Program.cs:69`) | WebApp | The storefront — Blazor Server (`MapRazorComponents<App>().AddInteractiveServerRenderMode()`, `src/WebApp/Program.cs:30`); also proxies product images to catalog-api (`src/WebApp/Program.cs:32`) |
| `webhooksclient` (`Program.cs:65`) | WebhookClient | Blazor Server demo client for webhooks (`src/WebhookClient/Program.cs:25`) |

**Plus one YARP reverse proxy and three containers:**
- `mobile-bff` — an Aspire-hosted YARP resource (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:60-62`), routing `/catalog-api/...`, ordering, and identity traffic for the mobile clients (`src/eShop.AppHost/Extensions.cs:185-220`).
- `redis` (`Program.cs:7`), `eventbus` RabbitMQ (`Program.cs:8-9`), and `postgres` using the `ankane/pgvector` image (`Program.cs:10-13`), which hosts four databases: `catalogdb`, `identitydb`, `orderingdb`, `webhooksdb` (`Program.cs:15-18`).
- Optionally OpenAI/Azure OpenAI or an Ollama container, both **off by default** (`useOpenAI = false` at `Program.cs:80`, `useOllama = false` at `Program.cs:86`).

## What does *not* start with the solution

**ClientApp and HybridApp are not launched by the AppHost.** They are .NET MAUI apps (`src/ClientApp/ClientApp.csproj:4`, `src/HybridApp/HybridApp.csproj:4-16`) with `MauiProgram.CreateMauiApp()` entry points, are absent from the AppHost's `AddProject` calls and project references, and are excluded from `eShop.Web.slnf`. They are deployed to devices/emulators separately and reach the backend through the `mobile-bff` proxy — HybridApp hardcodes `http://localhost:11632/` (`src/HybridApp/MauiProgram.cs:9`).

## How composition works

Two mechanisms, layered:

1. **Aspire service discovery / config injection.** `WithReference` injects connection strings and service endpoints (e.g. `webapp` references basket, catalog, ordering, rabbitmq at `Program.cs:72-75`), and `WithEnvironment` wires identity URLs. Note the deliberate cycle: identity-api gets callback URLs for all five clients (`Program.cs:96-101`), while those clients get `IdentityUrl` pointing back at it.
2. **RabbitMQ integration events.** Services are decoupled publisher/subscriber pairs — 13 message consumers across Basket.API, Catalog.API, Ordering.API, PaymentProcessor, WebApp, and Webhooks.API (e.g. `OrderStartedIntegrationEventHandler` in Basket.API, `GracePeriodConfirmedIntegrationEventHandler` in Ordering.API), built on the shared `EventBus`/`EventBusRabbitMQ` libraries.

Shared, non-runnable libraries: `eShop.ServiceDefaults` (telemetry/health/service-discovery, called as `AddServiceDefaults()`/`AddBasicServiceDefaults()` in every host), `EventBus`, `EventBusRabbitMQ`, `IntegrationEventLogEF`, `Ordering.Domain`, `Ordering.Infrastructure`, and `WebAppComponents` (Razor class library shared by WebApp and HybridApp).

One caveat worth flagging: `README.md:12` says "based on .NET 9", but every project actually targets `net10.0` — the README is stale on that point.
